metadata.title: Five Tests
metadata.purpose: Show that 'workspace' is not a metaphor — it's five falsifiable behavioral properties, and the paper tests all five, wrinkles included.
metadata.gate: GATE P — moot (Kokoro free); audio not yet generated

props.command: A global workspace is supposed to do five specific jobs: support verbal report, take top-down modulation, mediate reasoning, generalize flexibly, and stay out of automatic habits. Test Anthropic's J-space against all five — and show me where it wobbles.
props.runningText: composer types the ask — no narration

beats.narration_text: In the brain, the global workspace isn't a vibe. It's a job description — five functions. Anthropic ran all five against the J-space. Here's the scorecard, wrinkles included.
Verbal report. Directed modulation. Internal reasoning. Flexible generalization. And selectivity — flexible cognition in, automatic habit out. Five claims, each with its own experiment.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 1: five panels labeled verbal report / directed modulation / internal reasoning / flexible generalization / selectivity, drawn as five stations around a hub

beats.new_visual_element: five-station hub diagram — five workspace properties

beats.narration_text: Test one, verbal report. Inject a concept into the activations — nowhere in the text — then ask the model to introspect. If the concept lands in the J-space, the model can say it. The J-space component of the vector is the part that's reportable.

graphic.description: Test 1: a concept vector injected across the user turn; the model's introspection bubble reports it; J-space component highlighted

beats.new_visual_element: concept vector injection → introspection reports it

beats.narration_text: Test two, modulation. Tell the model to concentrate on citrus fruits while it copies an unrelated sentence, and the lens at mid-word reads orange — with lemon close behind. Tell it the fruits are irrelevant, ignore them —

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 9/10 design: the model copies 'The old painting hung crookedly on the wall' while instructed to concentrate on citrus fruits; lens at 'ook' reads orange, lemon; three conditions — no instruction / focus / ignore — shown as bar columns

beats.new_visual_element: citrus-focus bar chart — three conditions at mid-word lens

beats.narration_text: — and here's the wrinkle the authors kept in. Under 'ignore,' the concept still activates — less than under 'focus,' but the baseline was zero. Telling it not to think about the bear puts the bear in the room. Psychologists have a name for that: the white-bear effect. The machine has it too.

graphic.description: the ignore condition's bar: above zero, below focus — labelled honestly; a polar bear silhouette watermark fades in behind the chart

beats.skeptic_caption: Suppression is partial — remember this in episode five.
beats.new_visual_element: ignore-condition bar above zero; polar bear silhouette watermark

beats.narration_text: Test three, reasoning. Give it a question with a hidden middle step, and the middle step shows up in the workspace — unspoken, on schedule.

graphic.description: Test 3: 'The capital of the country where the Eiffel Tower stands is ___' style two-hop question; the unspoken intermediate (France) surfaces in the midlayer lens, then the answer (Paris) appears at output

beats.new_visual_element: two-hop question: hidden intermediate surfaces at midlayer

beats.narration_text: Arithmetic makes it visible: compute four plus seventeen times two plus seven, and twenty-one appears in the lens first, then the product — later layers, in the order the math requires. The workspace runs in computation order, not reading order.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 17: '(4+17)*2+7=' — A+B=21 surfaces at earlier layers, then ×2=42, at successively later layers; layer-axis timeline shows computation order

beats.new_visual_element: Fig 17: arithmetic intermediates appear in computation order across layers

beats.narration_text: Now the causal test. Swap the intermediate's lens coordinates and the answer should follow. Across sixteen function templates it works in seventy-six of one hundred ninety-two swaps at natural strength — one hundred one when you push harder. Real causality, forty to fifty percent reliability. Both halves of that sentence matter.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 15-left + Fig 19-left as one animated tally: swap successes across models; counts 76/192 top-1 and 101/192 at α=2 ticked up honestly on a running scoreboard

beats.skeptic_caption: A 40–53% hit rate proves the mechanism exists — not that it's the whole mechanism.

beats.narration_text: Split the probe for the hidden concept into the piece inside the J-space and the piece outside. The piece inside carries most of the causal punch. The workspace isn't just where thoughts are visible — it's where they do their work.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 16 logic: intermediate probe decomposed into J-space component (large arrow) and complement (small arrow); causal effect bar follows J-space component

beats.new_visual_element: probe split: J-space component carries the causal effect

beats.narration_text: Test four, generalization. One swap, planted once, redirects every downstream task that touches the concept — capital, language, anthem. That's the point of a workspace: write once, every specialist reads it.

graphic.description: Test 4: one France-to-Germany swap propagating across 16 templates (capital → Berlin, language → German, anthem → different, cuisine → different…); hub-and-spoke fan showing one write, many reads

beats.narration_text: Test five is the beautiful one. Delete the workspace — project out the top lens directions across the middle layers — and watch which abilities die.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 22+24 design: layer band shading for light/medium/heavy ablation strength; task battery performance bars falling as ablation deepens; normalized to unablated Sonnet 4.5; gray Haiku 4.5 reference floor

beats.new_visual_element: ablation battery: task bars collapse as workspace deleted

beats.narration_text: Flexible cognition collapses — the multi-hop reasoning, the ciphers, the constrained writing. Automatic cognition barely notices — the grammar keeps flowing, the habits keep firing. That dissociation is the workspace signature. In humans, it's the difference between what you do consciously and what you do on autopilot.

graphic.description: two-column split: FLEXIBLE column (multi-hop, ciphers, sonnets) bars collapsing to near-zero; AUTOMATIC column (fluent text, simple recall) bars surviving near baseline

beats.new_visual_element: selective collapse: flexible dies, automatic survives

beats.narration_text: And within the workspace, active work crowds out idle holding. Two concepts merely held in mind share tokens at chance. A concept and a computed answer almost never do — nine percent, against a twenty-nine percent baseline. Computation elbows storage aside.

graphic.description: rebuild Fig 73b: co-occupancy rates as paired bars — two held concepts 0.46 vs 0.53 control (near-chance); concept vs computed answer 0.09 vs 0.29 baseline (strongly below chance)

beats.narration_text: The scorecard: five for five on direction — with the wobbles stated, not hidden. The ignore instruction leaks. The swaps land half the time. The authors print both. That's what earns the rest of the series.

props.title: Five workspace tests — honestly scored
props.sparkLine: Five for five. *White-bear note; 76/192 swaps — wobbles printed.

beats.narration_text: Verdict: the J-space passes all five tests a workspace has to pass, and the paper prints its own wrinkles — the white-bear leak, the half-rate swaps. Five for five, honestly scored.

artifactLines: Hidden steps surface in computation order.
Ablation kills flexible cognition, spares autopilot.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Ask for the sixth test — the experiment that could prove this isn't a workspace at all.

props.command: Design a sixth test: an experiment that could show the J-space is NOT a global workspace. State the prediction global workspace theory makes, the result that would falsify it, and why none of the paper's five tests already covers it.
